Recorded
1959 on Commons; 11–⁠12 October 1958 in the Richter discography. Disputed: sources disagree

The Commons filename and date field say 1959, with no support for the 1 January day. The discography identifies a 1958 session with the same soloist, conductor and orchestra. The carrier underlying the Commons file has not been independently matched, so both dates remain visible.

  • 1959 — Commons attribution; day and month unestablished.
  • 11–⁠12 October 1958 — Richter chronology, SR-C#023.

The composer died in 1856. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

[4] [5]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons applies PD-EU-audio to Richter/Rowicki’s DG recording attributed to 1959. The dossier preserves the competing 1958 session attribution; both precede 1963. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.
